He focuses on the national security side of the Justice beat, including counterterrorism, counterintelligence and transnational repression. Before joining NPR, Lucas worked for a decade as a foreign correspondent for The Associated Press based in Poland, Egypt and Lebanon. In Poland, he covered the fallout from the revelations about secret CIA prisons in Eastern Europe. In the Middle East, he reported on the ouster of Hosni Mubarak in 2011 and the turmoil that followed. He also covered the Libyan civil war, the Syrian conflict and the rise of the Islamic State. He reported from Iraq during the U.S. occupation and later during the Islamic State takeover of Mosul in 2014. He also covered intelligence and national security for Congressional Quarterly. Lucas earned a bachelor's degree from The College of William and Mary, and a master's degree from Jagiellonian University in Krakow, Poland. Ryan Peay Ryan Peay, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Strategic Resources Ryan Peay is the Deputy Assistant Secretary for the Office of Strategic Resources in the Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office. He sets the strategic direction for the Office and administers its Global Energy Security and Strategic Petroleum Reserve programs, including the associated analysis, budget, and natural gas regulation efforts. He also leads the Department’s engagement with the National Petroleum Council federal advisory committee. Previously, Mr. Peay was the Deputy Assistant Secretary for the Office of Oil and Natural Gas, where he led the Department’s oil, gas, and critical minerals R&D portfolio. Prior to joining the U.S. Department of Energy, Mr. Peay was a manager at a major consulting firm, focused on strategic planning, financial programming, and budgeting activities. From 2002 to 2007, Mr. Peay served on active duty in the U.S. Army as a Field Artillery Officer in the 101st Airborne Division. Mr. Peay holds a Master of Business Administration (MBA) from the Darden School of Business at the University of Virginia and is a graduate of the Virginia Military Institute with a B.A. in International Studies and Political Science. May 7, 2024 Safe Handling of Human Remains of VHF Patients in U.S. Hospitals and Mortuaries Key points Viruses that cause VHFs can be transmitted in postmortem care settings through unsafe handling of remains. Safely handle human remains by properly using personal protective equipment (PPE) and specific body bags, and by following decontamination measures at every step of the process. Only trained personnel wearing recommended PPE should touch or move any human remains from a person who has died from VHFs. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Safety and Conditions It’s no secret: Outdoor recreation is gaining popularity on the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument (GSENM), but it is especially important to understand that ultimately – your safety is your responsibility. That said, planning is an important step in being prepared and ready for your adventure. Remember, the Monument can be very unforgiving, and its wild character should not be underestimated. And although overnight stays on the monument do not require a permit, free permits are available at any of the local Visitor Centers and are highly encouraged. The permit system can become crucial in the case of a search and rescue . Below are some best practices to keep in mind when recreating on the GSENM: It’s always a good idea to let people know your itinerary and when you expect be back Travel in groups rather than by yourself Before beginning any of your Monument adventures, make sure you've planned your way in, and planned your way out Know the extended weather forecast Carry extra clothing, blankets, food and water for emergencies Remember, cell phone coverage across the Monument is sparse if at all Plan Ahead and Prepare

But his possession of “Uncle Tom’s Cabin” turned him into an abolitionist hero Green, from an illustration published in 1872 Wood Etching from William Still’s 1872 book “The Underground Railroad” Wikimedia Green, from an illustration published in 1872 Wood Etching from William Still’s 1872 book “The Underground Railroad” Wikimedia The knock on Samuel Green’s door must have felt inevitable. It was April 1857, and in the past decade hundreds of Black Marylanders had slipped off the farms and plantations where they were enslaved. Now local white leaders were beginning to suspect that Green knew more about the runaways than he let on. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn San Juan Islands National Monument Situated in the northern reaches of Washington State's Puget Sound, the San Juan Islands are a uniquely beautiful archipelago of over 450 islands, rocks, and pinnacles. The San Juan Islands National Monument encompasses approximately 1,000 acres of land spread across many of these rocks and islands and managed by the Department of the Interior's Bureau of Land Management. Drawing visitors from around the world, this is a landscape of unmatched contrasts, where forests seem to spring from gray rock and distant, snow-capped peaks provide the backdrop for sandy beaches. The San Juan Islands National Monument is a trove of scientific and historic treasures, a refuge for an array of wildlife, and a classroom for generations of Americans. On March 25, 2013, President Obama signed a proclamation to designate the San Juan Islands National Monument. The proclamation states that, "The protection of these lands in the San Juan Islands will maintain their historical and cultural significance and enhance their unique and varied natural and scientific resources, for the benefit of all Americans." Fresh evidence from Cameron Bancroft - the culprit of the ball-tampering in South Africa in 2018 - has heaped pressure on Australia captain Pat Cummins, former coach Darren Lehmann and Cricket Australia. pages.text: Santander, Spain: A 2027 Guide to Its Waterfront Art Museums | National Geographic TRAVEL BEST OF THE WORLD Beloved by Spaniards, Santander Is Becoming a Global Art Mecca The easygoing beachfront city is getting a host of new and reborn museums. A 2014 transformation by landscape architect Fernando Caruncho more than doubled the size of Pereda Gardens, in the historic heart of Santander. Luis Fonseca, Getty Images By Eddi Fiegel Published October 20, 2026 Santander, a port city in northwestern Spain, has long seduced Spaniards with its spectacular horseshoe bay surrounded by rolling green hills and the Cantabrian mountains in the distance. But now the city, the capital of the Cantabria region, is poised to become an international art destination. In September 2026, the new arts, culture, and technology center Faro Santander opened in a historic building redesigned by acclaimed British architect David Chipperfield with a permanent collection including works by such legendary figures as el Greco, Rubens, Velázquez, and Goya. ( See all 25 of the destinations that made our list of the best places to visit in 2027. ) Meanwhile, 2027 will bring the first outpost of Madrid’s renowned Reina Sofía museum. The impressive Museum of Prehistory and Archaeology of Cantabria also has a new home designed by the Barcelona-based architecture practice Mendoza Partida. Art lovers are sure to appreciate the city’s walkable city center—where ornate, neoclassical façades sit alongside Baroque churches and grand, porticoed squares—and the wide sandy beaches lined with elegant fin-de-siècle villas.

pages.text: Sarina Wiegman contract: Why England manager faces biggest challenge yet - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Sarina Wiegman has won the past three Women's European Championships - with the Netherlands in 2017 and England in 2022 and 2025 By Joe Bradshaw BBC Sport senior journalist Published 19 October 2026 When Sarina Wiegman took the reins as England manager in September 2021, she declared she had "come to bring the next level". Winner of the 2017 Women's Euros with her own Netherlands and runner-up at the subsequent World Cup in 2019, she certainly had the pedigree, but could she deliver on her promises? Five years on, Wiegman has pocketed two more European Championships and acquired another silver medal on the global stage. Not only that, but the success of her Lionesses exploded the women's game in this country, taking it not just to a new level, but to previously unthinkable heights. And yet on the day Wiegman extends her deal until after the Euros in 2029, her newest challenge could be her hardest yet. England manager Wiegman signs contract extension Published 19 October Why must England evolve? Wiegman's successful England teams have been built on a core group of players from an outstanding generation - but a few cracks have appeared this year. Seven of the team that started against world champions Spain in June also played in the Euro 2022 final against Germany - and their 4-0 defeat in Mallorca laid bare the gap England must bridge to the world's best. That result also consigned England to two rounds of play-offs to reach next summer's World Cup.

pages.text: Save time getting through airport security with Trusted Traveler Programs | USAGov Skip to main content Save time getting through airport security with Trusted Traveler Programs Trusted Traveler Programs can help reduce airport security and border crossing wait times. Learn about applying for programs like TSA Precheck and Global Entry and managing memberships. What are the Trusted Traveler Programs, and how do you apply? The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) manages the Trusted Traveler Programs. These include TSA Precheck and Global Entry . As a pre-approved member, you can use expedited lanes at U.S. airports and when entering the U.S. by land or sea. TSA Precheck is for travelers departing from U.S. airports. Global Entry is for travelers entering the U.S. from international destinations by air, land, or sea. There are also programs for entering the U.S. from Canada and Mexico. To apply, you will need to pay a fee and provide documents proving your identity. Depending on the program, you may need to complete an interview. If approved, your program membership will last 5 years. Saving Electricity The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) is deeply committed to saving electricity across all sectors through various initiatives, recognizing its vital role in national energy policy and sustainability. This commitment is reflected in the establishment and updating of energy efficiency standards for appliances and equipment which are projected to yield significant annual savings and reduce carbon emissions. DOE's Role in Electricity Conservation The Department of Energy (DOE) is instrumental in saving electricity, driven by its core mission to promote energy conservation and independence since 1977. It achieves this through a multi-pronged approach: establishing policies and standards, including new energy efficiency standards for appliances and federal building codes, which are projected to save billions and reduce carbon emissions. DOE also funds and manages significant programs like the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI) and the Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP), which expands renewable energy and helps low-income households improve energy efficiency. Yet you may not realize that probably the most expensive thing you will ever buy in your lifetime is your…retirement. Perhaps you've never thought of "buying" your retirement. Yet that is exactly what you do when you put money into a retirement nest egg. You are paying today for the cost of your retirement tomorrow. The cost of those future years is getting more expensive for most Americans, for two reasons. First, we live longer after we retire – with many of us spending 15, 25, even 30 years in retirement – and we are more active. Second, you may have to shoulder a greater chunk of the cost of your retirement because fewer companies are providing traditional pension plans. How can we protect them? In 2022, Anicet Etekpo, a security officer in Benin, clicked on a Facebook link sent by someone he believed was a friend. "The link led me to a fraudulent platform that asked for my personal information, including my bank account," he told the BBC. Etekpo suffered a significant financial loss and began to question the security of his personal data. He had only been online for a few years when the incident happened. As internet connectivity expands in places like West Africa, millions will encounter online risks like his for the first time. How can they be protected? An estimated 2.6 billion people – roughly a third of the global population – currently have no access to the internet. If connectivity continues to increase at its current rate, approximately two billion more people will gain access to the web by 2030. pages.description:
A Schematron report tells you if there’s a metadata quality issue with your records.

Schematron is a pattern-based XML validation language. We try to stop the deposit of metadata with obvious issues, but we can’t catch everything because publication practices are so varied. For example, most family names in our database that end with jr are the result of a publisher including a suffix (Jr) in a family name, but there are of course surnames ending with ‘jr’.
